name: Ethiopia: Misty Valley, Yirgacheffe
cupping_notes: Blueberry, chocolate, strawberry, floral, clean, balanced body. Bright lemon drop sweetness.
description: Ethiopia prepares some of the world’s finest coffee, known for complexity and delicious flavor profiles you can’t find anywhere else. From roasting connoisseurs to casual coffee lovers, our customers adore the versatility of this bean. Find out why this coffee always sells out! Producer, exporter, and cultivator Abdullah Bagersh ensures that Misty Valley’s ripe cherries are subject to superior care from start to finish. Through the first 48 hours, the coffee beans are constantly turned to provide even evaporation. This process provides consistency and cleanliness, which is often difficult to accomplish in the Gedio region of Ethiopia. The resulting speak for themselves! Cupping Notes : Blueberry, chocolate, strawberry, floral, clean, balanced body. Bright lemon drop sweetness.

name: Costa Rica: La Minita Estate, Tarrazu
cupping_notes: Brilliant acidity, a medium body, and sweet flavors of orange citrus, caramelized sugar, and fine chocolate. It is impeccably balanced with a long, satisfying finish.
description: Each coffee parcel differentiates from its neighbors by having its own micro-climate, but the Costa Rica La Minta is not combined with any other farms in a cooperative scenario. Each coffee is milled by itself to maintain integrity, and workers only pick cherries when they have fully ripened. The farm uses acclaimed gardening techniques all by hand. The La Minita Tarrazu sports beautiful honeysuckle-like blossoms after the initial rain and its birthplace is considered one of the best coffee origins in the world. A Rainforest Certified Alliance coffee, these beans come with the guarantee of a better life for the people and land it comes from––better infrastructure, a more sustainable ecosystem, farming education, and gender equality. Estate owners watch over every process to ensure every bean you roast reaches perfection. Cupping Notes: Brilliant acidity, a medium body, and sweet flavors of orange citrus, caramelized sugar, and fine chocolate. It is impeccably balanced with a long, satisfying finish.

name: Bolivia: Organic Caranavi FTO, La Paz Department
local_region: Caranavi & Apolo Province La Paz municipality
cupping_notes: Super sweet caramel, milk chocolate, rounded but heavy body with mild orange acidity in the undertones makes this an extremely balanced cup that is versatile and can be used for drip, cold brew, or a single origin espresso. Probably best roasted to a nice medium.
description: The Caranavi is a specialty Bolivian coffee grown by a small group of native coffee farmers known as colonials, on land that is at high elevations rising to 8,500 feet above sea level. These coffee beans are cultivated in the tropical growing regions of Bolivia below a magnificent forest, coming from 41 small farms averaging about three acres each. This cooperative is comprised of all indigenous people, that are native to the land on the edge of the Andes mountains and bordering the rain forest and jungle of the Amazon. The land next to their farms is government-protected land, and the indigenous groups have decided to treat their land as if it were protected as well. Most of which have already been certified Smithsonian Bird Friendly, and all of which have been certified Organic. Cupping Notes: Super sweet caramel, milk chocolate, rounded but heavy body with mild orange acidity in the undertones makes this an extremely balanced cup that is versatile and can be used for drip, cold brew, or a single origin espresso. Probably best roasted to a nice medium.

name: Tanzania Peaberry, Kilimanjaro
cupping_notes: Sweet brown sugar honey aroma, juicy smooth medium to full body, clean, sweet, fruity lingering aftertaste, exotic well, balanced, intense flavor, and crisp, bright, tangy winey acidity with black tea, citrus, orange, and blueberry notes. Tanzania peaberry coffee gets a lot of attention because the bean looks different, but shape alone doesn't tell you whether the coffee will taste better. A typical cherry develops two seeds with flat sides facing each other, while a peaberry forms when only one seed develops and ends up rounder. That difference is real, although the usual claims that peaberry must be sweeter, rarer, more caffeinated, or automatically higher quality go much further than the evidence supports. For a home roaster, the useful questions are more practical: where was the lot grown, how was it processed, what do the cupping notes say, and how does the smaller rounded bean move in your machine? Coffee Bean Corral currently lists Tanzania Peaberry, Kilimanjaro at $8.15 per pound and available to add to cart as of August 29, 2026, so you can evaluate a real current lot instead of a generic peaberry myth. Key Takeaways Peaberry describes seed development and shape: One seed develops in the cherry rather than the more common pair, producing a rounder bean. It isn't automatically better: Farm, variety, cherry selection, processing, drying, storage, roast, and brewing still determine quality. Shape can matter in the roaster: Rounded beans can move differently in a drum or agitation system, so watch evenness and don't assume a standard flat-bean profile transfers perfectly. Tanzania is strongly associated with peaberry sorting: Coffee Bean Corral's current lot combines coffees from producers in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha areas. Current availability has changed: The live product is available as of August 29, 2026, so older sold-out references should not control the buying recommendation. What Is Peaberry Coffee? Peaberry coffee forms when one rounded seed develops inside the cherry instead of the more common pair that flatten against each other. A recent Scientific Reports paper describes the same single-seed form, which matters because it gives us a precise botanical definition without turning the shape into a quality claim. Once the coffee is harvested, peaberries can be separated during grading because their size and shape differ from regular flat beans. That can give a roaster a more physically consistent screen of round seeds, but it still doesn't tell you whether the cherries were picked ripe, processed cleanly, stored well, or roasted well, so shape remains only one part of the buying decision. Is Peaberry Better Than Regular Coffee? No, not inherently. Peaberry shape can influence sorting and may change how the beans move or receive heat in a particular roaster, but cup quality still comes from genetics, farm conditions, cherry selection, processing, drying, storage, roast execution, and brewing. If those fundamentals are weak, a rounder seed doesn't rescue the coffee. The "peaberry is sweeter because one bean gets all the nutrients" story is popular because it sounds intuitive, but it isn't a strong basis for buying decisions. Research has found physical and chemical differences in some samples without establishing a universal sensory advantage, so treat peaberry as one characteristic among many. If the lot has clean processing, useful producer information, compelling cupping notes, and a profile that suits your roaster, those are much better reasons to buy it. Why Tanzania Is Known for Peaberry Coffee Tanzania is one of the origins most strongly associated with commercially separated peaberry lots, especially around Kilimanjaro and Arusha, so buyers often encounter the shape and the country together. That association is useful for shopping, but it shouldn't turn into a flavor shortcut because producer mix, variety, process, elevation, and roast still change the cup from one lot to the next. Names such as Kilimanjaro and Arusha appear often in the market, but a modern product may combine coffee from many small producers rather than represent one estate. How to Roast Peaberry Coffee Don't assume peaberry needs a completely different roast profile, but do give the first batch enough attention to learn how the shape behaves in your machine. Rounded beans may move differently in a drum or agitation system, and because size and density can vary by lot, your familiar flat-bean profile may need a small heat or airflow adjustment rather than a wholesale rewrite. Start with a familiar load and a moderate profile. You want enough early energy to establish steady momentum, but don't use an aggressive charge simply because the beans look small. Watch the coffee's color and smell through drying and browning, then approach first crack with control. A useful test routine is: Use your normal sample or test-batch size. Keep machine behavior familiar. Watch bean movement. In a drum, round beans may roll differently; in an air roaster, fluidization and density can affect movement. Track evenness. If the surface colors are diverging, adjust agitation, airflow, or heat rather than simply extending the roast. Listen to first crack, but don't depend on sound alone. A smaller bean can produce a different acoustic pattern from coffees you know. Choose development by cup goal. Preserve tea, citrus, and blueberry with restraint, or develop further for more brown-sugar and body emphasis. Cool quickly and cup. Your first batch is a baseline, not a verdict. name: Peru: Organic Finca La Esperanza G1, San Martin
cupping_notes: Chocolate & cherry, toasty, nutty, and sweet aroma. Notes of citrus, malt, pine, and semi-sweet chocolate with a mild, lingering aftertaste, low acidity, full-bodied, and well-balanced.
description: Shade-grown and younger than six years old (within its first few seasons of production), the Finca La Esperanza is sourced from a 2.5-acre family farm in San Martin’s Soritor village. The producer, Walter Gutierrez, purchased the once-abandoned Finca La Esperanza in 2007 and transformed it into a marvelous spot for Peru organic coffee to flourish. The Finca La Esperanza coffee is grown alongside corn and cocoa, proving the previous owner wrong and showing anything is possible. Finca La Esperanza’s cup profile has only improved with the farmers’ ever-growing education and organic certification throughout the years. Coffee is Peru’s most prominent agricultural commodity, and it is the ninth-largest arabica producer in the world. Peru is also an organic coffee hotspot––there are 220,000 organic coffee farms––and high elevations with just the right amount of shade in the Northern Andes. Since farmers traditionally use all-natural methods when growing their beans (natural fertilizer, chemical/pesticide avoidance, and recycling coffee pulp, mulch, and other substances), it was only fitting that they strive for organic coffee excellence. Because of their efforts, the area is known as a sanctuary for birds and other docile wildlife in the balanced ecosystem, and San Martin’s rainforest is abundant with fertile soil. Cupping Notes : Chocolate & cherry, toasty, nutty, and sweet aroma. Notes of citrus, malt, pine, and semi-sweet chocolate with a mild, lingering aftertaste, low acidity, full-bodied, and well-balanced.

name: Colombia: Supremo EP, Huila
cupping_notes: Well balanced acidity and a delicate medium body. It starts off sweet with notes of tart fruit and finishes with a bittersweet, dark cocoa notes.
description: A 17/18 screen (Supremo), the Colombia Huila is smaller-bodied when compared to its relative, the Bucaramanga. Grown and harvested in Huila, Colombia, this bean’s origin lies near the Nevado de Huila volcano––the soil is rich with minerals, and the microclimate is perfect for perfect, complex coffee. The producers use manual, hand-cranked machines to de-pulp the bean’s cherry, and raised beds dry the coffee evenly. The beans are expertly handled at every processing stage Cupping Notes: Well balanced acidity and a delicate medium body. It starts off sweet with notes of tart fruit and finishes with a bittersweet, dark cocoa notes.

name: Mexico: La Laja Honey, Tlaltetela, Veracruz
cupping_notes: This coffee is supremely sweet with a mild orange citric acidity and a smooth, creamy body. It is very clean and consistent.
description: La Laja, a family farm and mining group in Veracruz, Mexico, began in 1920 when its founder, Hermilo Sampieri, bought his first coffee farm in Huatusco. His son joined in, and eventually, one farm became seven––Finca La Laja, Finca El Mirador, Finca Las Palmas, Finca La Veracruz, and three other farms in Puebla. La Laja also purchases a wide variety of cherries from small farmers in Chiapas. They are experts in processing, and they own wet and dry mills. La Laja’s honey-processed bean has its skin removed, but the sugary pulp remains through fermentation to add a sweet flavor. After de-pulping, this coffee dries for up to 20 days on covered raised beds. Cupping notes: This coffee is supremely sweet with a mild orange citric acidity and a smooth, creamy body. It is very clean and consistent.

name: Brazil: Oberon, Cerrado
cupping_notes: Chocolate, nutty, fruity aftertaste; light acidity, sweet, full body. Clean and balanced.
description: New harvest arrival: 10/02/2026 Brazil’s Oberon coffee is a pure Cerrado blend that perfectly captures what the region is known for in one sip––blissful temperatures averaging 68 degrees Fahrenheit, altitudes reaching just below 1,250, and an average rainfall of 1,600 millimeters ––a haven for healthy coffee trees. The Cerrado land houses just over 140,000 hectares of coffee production that vary in size from 100 hectares to 3,000––all dedicated to consistent cup quality. Cupping notes : Chocolate, nutty, fruity aftertaste; light acidity, sweet, full body. Clean and balanced.

name: Guatemala: La Flor Del Cafe, Antigua
cupping_notes: The aroma is rich, dark, chocolate, classic on the nose. The acidity is low to medium, and the body is full. This is a very balanced cup. The flavor is subtle, dark, mocha notes, and rich.
description: New arrival: 10/02/2026 Our Antigua bean is washed, sun-dried, and hand-sorted in the modernized Pastores mill up to 1,600 meters above sea level on small farms. Coming from one of the world’s top coffee-growing regions––Guatemala––the quality control is impeccable, with only the absolute cream of the crop chosen for export. It’s one of the most sought-after coffees in Antigua because it can handle a variety of roast styles, it has a lively, fruity flavor profile, and the perfect amount of acidity. Cupping Notes: The aroma is rich, dark, chocolate, classic on the nose. The acidity is low to medium, and the body is full. This is a very balanced cup. The flavor is subtle, dark, mocha notes, and rich.

name: Sumatra: Mandheling G1, Aceh
local_region: Batak Region of West-Central Sumatra, Aceh
cupping_notes: Chocolate, cedar, sweet tobacco, and spice, along with a mild acidity and creamy body.
description: This shade-grown Sumatran coffee is a classic, so steeped in the history of this Indonesian island that the name itself is not of a region, but rather the result of a language barrier. Sumatra Mandheling is grown on the slopes of Mount Leuser, a volcano near the port of Pandang, in the Batak area of Aceh. It is home to one of the most ancient ecosystems in the world! The flavor profile is vibrant and spicy, a heavy coffee reminiscent of the atmosphere on this tropical paradise. If you're looking for a Sumatran coffee that won't let you down, this is a go-to. Cupping Notes: Chocolate, cedar, sweet tobacco, and spice, along with a mild acidity and creamy body.

name: Guatemala: Organic Asdecafe SHB, Huehuetenango
cupping_notes: Tangerine, creamy, golden raisin, toffee.
description: Grown under guava, plantain, and banana trees in Guatemala’s Huehuetenango region, La Asociación Sostenible de Cafe de Guatemala (ASDECAFE) proudly produces a bean committed to sustainability, environmental protection, equitable distribution among its workers, and of course, the best coffee quality imaginable available internationally. With more than 1,000 active members today, ASDECAFE was founded in 2103 by only six farmers and continues to grow while becoming certified organic. Cupping Notes: Tangerine, creamy, golden raisin, toffee.

name: Uganda: Organic Bugisu, Sipi Falls
cupping_notes: A complex cup with notes of baker's chocolate, molasses, and black pepper. Minimal brightness, above average sweetness, and a pleasing, full body.
description: A coffee bean like no other grows on the verdant slopes of Africa’s oldest volcano, Mount Elgon––the Ugandan Organic Bugisu. Family farms source this bean, and it’s named after the people native to the area: the Bugisu. The Sipi Falls Coffee Project has been regulating this bean and providing support since 1999 and has evolved to protect over 2,000 hectares of production. Agronomic practices have constantly improved over the years in order to yield more coffee at its best quality through intercropping, which allows the beans to have the vital nutrients they need. Cupping Notes: A complex cup with notes of baker's chocolate, molasses, and black pepper. Minimal brightness, above average sweetness, and a pleasing, full body.

name: Peru: Organic La Florida, Selva Central
cupping_notes: Milk Chocolate, Pear, Toffee, with a full, creamy body, and mild acidity.
description: The La Florida Cooperative was established in 1965 by a group of small-scale farmers from the Chanchamayo region–since then, the organization has been committed to improving its coffee beans. For the past 13 years, La Florida has not only been dedicated to producing the highest quality beans but also strives to improve their quality of life – both for their people and the environment. The organization’s Fair Trade revenue brings education, healthcare, and infrastructure to an otherwise rural area – in fact, the Occupational Learning Center for Sustainable Agriculture was created due to their efforts. Cupping Notes: Milk Chocolate, Pear, Toffee, with a full, creamy body, and mild acidity.

name: Vietnam: Robusta, Central Highlands
description: Robusta coffee beans have spent years carrying a reputation they only partly deserve. A lot of commodity Robusta has been roasted dark, blended for cost, and brewed for intensity, so it’s easy to assume the species itself must be harsh or one-dimensional. But Coffea canephora , the species commonly sold as Robusta, covers a much wider quality range, and better processing can produce coffees that are cleaner, sweeter, and far more useful to a home roaster than the stereotype suggests. Robusta is especially interesting when you want more body, more caffeine, or a stronger espresso blend, although none of those benefits works in isolation. More crema doesn’t automatically mean better espresso, and higher caffeine doesn’t tell you whether you’ll enjoy the cup. The better question is what you want the Robusta to do. Coffee Bean Corral’s current Vietnam Robusta from the Central Highlands is washed, heavy-bodied, and available at $8.85 per pound as of August 29, 2026, which gives you a practical lot to test instead of arguing about the species in the abstract.

name: Kenya: Select Plus AA, Kiambu County
cupping_notes: Clean, well-balanced, intense flavor, smooth medium body, sweet lingering aftertaste, bright crisp acidity, and sweet brown sugar aroma with blueberry, raspberry, and black tea notes.
description: Our Kenya AA Select Plus is produced by a number of small farmers in the central Kenyan farmlands that surround Mt. Kenya. It is a single-origin coffee from the Nairobi Coffee Exchange and is considered some of the best quality coffee in the world! The Kenyan Process is a double fermentation method where the puled cherries are soaked twice in fermentation tanks and are sun-dried on raised beds for 1-2 weeks. The lots are consolidated at a local mill and go through a double fermentation method before being sun-dried on raised beds. The Nairobi Coffee Exchange grades the beans, cups the coffee, and sells it at auction, where we buy it for you. Cupping Notes: Clean, well-balanced, intense flavor, smooth medium body, sweet lingering aftertaste, bright crisp acidity, and sweet brown sugar aroma with blueberry, raspberry, and black tea notes.

name: Guatemala: HHT SHB, Huehuetenango
cupping_notes: Well balanced intense flavor, sweet brown sugar honey aroma, smooth medium body and clean sweet lingering aftertaste with bright crisp vibrant acidity, citrus, orange, lime, peach, apple and chocolate notes.
description: Huehuetenango sits in the western highlands of Guatemala, bordering Mexico. It was one of the most ethnically diverse regions in Guatemala, and coffee growing has a rich, deep history and ties to the land. This variety is a proven, popular coffee you shouldn't miss! Cupping Notes: Well balanced intense flavor, sweet brown sugar honey aroma, smooth medium body and clean sweet lingering aftertaste with bright crisp vibrant acidity, citrus, orange, lime, peach, apple and chocolate notes.

name: Ethiopia: Organic Limu G2, Oromia
cupping_notes: Bergamot citrus, jasmine, cherry
description: New arrival: Oct. '26 This grade 2 Ethiopian coffee from the Limu region is one of the most interesting coffees we've come across recently, and for an Ethiopian coffee, that's saying something! We cupped one sample and immediately knew we had to bring this one in. Jimma zone is located to the southwest of Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa. Much of Jimma, like other coffee-growing regions in Ethiopia, is a vast, gently sloping plateau with incredibly fertile soil at high elevations. The top-quality coffees from Jimma, especially those from the Limu, Gera, and Goma districts, are renowned for their vibrant and delicate fruit flavors. The region’s renowned "white" honey, collected by bees from the blossoms of coffee plants and the surrounding forests, is a well-known symbol of Jimma and brings immense pleasure to the senses. Coffees from this zone, along with those from the nearby Illubabor region, are often labeled as “Limu”, a distinction based more on terroir and shared flavor profiles rather than geographical boundaries. Cupping notes : Bergamot citrus, jasmine, cherry

name: Vietnam: Son La Select SHG, Son La
cupping_notes: Spicy, cocoa, and herbal notes with caramel and almond undertones; medium body, bright acidity; smooth finish with sweet aftertaste.
description: Son La's mountainous terrain and ideal climate conditions create perfect growing conditions for the hardy Catimor varietal, which thrives in this region without requiring irrigation. The cooperative behind this coffee is committed to sustainable farming practices and social responsibility, led by manager Ngoc Anh Sprunker, who also serves as Vietnam chapter chairperson of the International Women's Coffee Association. The washed processing method enhances the coffee's inherent brightness while maintaining its medium body and smooth character. This processing style allows the unique terroir of the Son La region to shine through, creating a cup that balances the spicy and herbal notes characteristic of Vietnamese highland coffees with the chocolatey richness that makes this coffee approachable for a wide range of palates. Cupping Notes: Spicy, cocoa, and herbal notes with caramel and almond undertones; medium body, bright acidity; smooth finish with sweet aftertaste.

name: Papua New Guinea: Mile High A, Eastern Highlands
cupping_notes: Bright acidity and creamy body with notes of berries, caramel, malt, and citrus.
description: The Mile High Papua New Guinea beans are grown in part by the Arokara Cooperative––a plantation partner with firm beliefs in chemical-free coffee production and updates to their processes annually. The Mile High is grown on the outskirts of Kainantu, which is a town in the Eastern Highlands of Papua New Guinea. Nearly 12,000 of Kainantu’s citizens depend on coffee processing to support their families, and as many as 60 assistants can be hired at one time. The farms sit at an altitude of 1,600 meters above sea level, and their sizes are modest. The Mile High beans are highly consistent and “clean” due to their washed nature––the cherries are de-pulped and hardly fermented. This way, any overbearing sweetness disappears. Cupping notes : Bright acidity and creamy body with notes of berries, caramel, malt, and citrus.

name: Kenya: Peaberry Plus 15/16, Kirinyaga County
local_region: Meru, Embu, Nyeri, Muranga, Kirinyaga, Kiambu, Kangundo
harvest: September- December (Main Crop); May- July (Fly Crop)
cupping_notes: Clean and well balanced with a smooth medium body, crisp and vibrant acidity and a sweet brown sugar aroma with flavor notes of orange, blackberry, grapefruit and nectarine.
description: This new Kenyan Peaberry Plus is grown in rich, volcanic soil with ample rainfall which is an ideal climate for the development of the aroma and flavor notes that this country's coffees are known for. The PB Plus refers to the smaller screen size, 15/16 and the quality of this bean. Most farms in this part of Kenya are found near the second tallest mountain in Africa- Mt. Kenya. Each country in this region has a number of small farms that work together to make up local grower association and cooperatives as well as larger estates which gives the country a diverse production base. Cupping Notes : Clean and well balanced with a smooth medium body, crisp and vibrant acidity and a sweet brown sugar aroma with flavor notes of orange, blackberry, grapefruit and nectarine.

name: Java: Blawan Estate, East Java
cupping_notes: A rich, medium-acidity coffee with a robust body and sweetness, with notes of vanilla, caramel, and black cherry.
description: The Kayumas Estate, or "Golden Wood", is located on the island of Java in Indonesia and was first established by the Dutch in the 18th century. This Estate is situated in the northeast area of the Bondowoso province of Java. Initially, coffee was cultivated in low-lying areas, but in the 19th Century, coffee leaf rust disease destroyed most of their production, forcing new coffee cultivation into the highland plateaus where higher altitudes and volcanic soil provided perfect growing conditions. The Kayumas coffee is grown in East Java, on a government-run estate where the coffee is handpicked and then processed using the fully washed method – this gives the coffee a cleaner profile than other Indonesian coffees. Cupping Notes: A rich, medium-acidity coffee with a robust body and sweetness, with notes of vanilla, caramel, and black cherry.

name: Colombia: Decaf EA, Cauca
cupping_notes: Candy-like, with notes of tropical fruit and citrus; creamy body.
description: Processed with ethyl acetate, (a sweet-smelling organic compound derived from sugar cane created during fermentation) this bean originates from the Andean region’s only decaffeination plant, Descafecol. The plant relies on pure water from the Navado el Ris (a snow-capped volcano resting on the border of Caldas and Tolima) and natural ethyl acetate from sugar cane plants in Palmira, Colombia. From the Trilladora Andes Mill, the coffee’s complete process involves machine-pulping, 6-8 hour fermentation, rinsing and patio-drying for 12 hours, and a final 6-hour drying. The Decaffeination process starts with steaming the green coffee beans at low pressure in order to remove their silver skins. Then, the beans are swelled and softened with hot water, which starts the caffeine's hydrolysis process––water causes the caffeine to break down and separate from the other compounds. In the next step, the ethyl acetate circulates through the beans until at least 97% of the caffeine is removed. Saturated steam is applied at low pressure to remove the ethyl acetate in the final processing stages. Coffee beans are then cooled to ambient temperature, surrounded by fans, and polished with carnauba wax, protecting the beans from humidity. The coffee beans are vacuum-dried in drums to ensure water removal and bring moisture levels to less than 12%. Cupping notes : Candy-like, with notes of tropical fruit and citrus; creamy body.

name: CBC Blend: Ferdelance
description: Created by Russ as the perfect single shot, our own Ferdelance blend is one of our favorites for espresso––plenty of crema and lots of nutty richness. While its namesake isn’t precisely straight from Central America’s deadly viper, this mix is still high octane, and it packs a potent, complex bite! It's a potent blend (roasted dark), but also sweet when roasted lighter, and develops a thick crema. Deep and rich-flavored with heavy body and the balance you might expect from a blend so long in development. Roast it lighter and enjoy a creamy chocolate espresso drink with a dominant nutty taste, or take it to the limit and get the bittersweet end of the spectrum. Very versatile and quite complex.

name: Honduras: Kingdom Growers SHG, Montecillos
cupping_notes: Well balanced, sweet citrus fragrance, good acidity with sweet orange flavor, molasses, and a creamy body and finish.
description: A breathtaking Honduran coffee that has won and placed top three for America’s Best Cold Brew Competition, Honduras Kingdom Growers can be found on the Montecillos Mountain Range’s extraordinary slopes, where a cooperative of small coffee growers are dedicated to producing high-quality, sustainable coffee as a community. Each year, the Honduras Kingdom Growers cooperative works with nearly 200 small farm holders and provides them with access to an expanding eco-friendly knowledge base––this gives the farm holders a variety of training and farm-management resources, including processing and milling techniques to ensure a fantastic bean is produced. Honduras Kingdom Growers farmers use teamwork to produce more yields while simultaneously raising income for the people’s benefit. In Honduras, high-grade, specialty coffee is an ever-growing need. Thus, the Honduran farms range from one to twelve acres in size and spread between elevations of 4,000 to 5,2000 feet. Bean lots are hand-picked and processed together to ensure the highest quality cup. La Paz, Comayagua, Santa Barbara, and Intibucá are locales within the Montecillos region––IHCAFE (The Honduran Institute of Coffee) defines the peachy Montecillos as one of the six major coffee-growing regions in Honduras. Cupping Notes : Well balanced, sweet citrus fragrance, good acidity with sweet orange flavor, molasses, and a creamy body and finish.

name: Nicaragua: Las Segovias Coop SHG, San Juan del Rio Coco
cupping_notes: Clean well balanced flavor, smooth medium body, sweet brown sugar aroma, sweet aftertaste and bright crisp acidity with apple, lemon, pear, peach and chocolate notes.
description: Specialty coffee in Nicaragua is built around small farm cooperatives, supporting each other and helping to maintain high quality from seed to ship! And the producers in San Juan del Rio Coco is no different. These producers use traditional organic farming practices on small plots of land, where they cultivate coffee alongside shade trees, bananas, corn, and beans. During the harvest, each producer engages in selective picking, focusing on harvesting only fully ripened cherries, which are then processed using the farm's micro-mill. The cherries undergo washing and floating to remove damaged and less dense coffee beans. The selected cherries are then de-pulped, fermented, washed, gently dried, and stored until they are ready for export. Cupping Notes: Clean well balanced flavor, smooth medium body, sweet brown sugar aroma, sweet aftertaste and bright crisp acidity with apple, lemon, pear, peach and chocolate notes.

name: Guatemala: Finca Vallure, Huehuetenango
cupping_notes: Honey, floral and citrus with dark chocolate.
description: Guatemala HHT Finca Vallaure SHB This fully washed coffee was grown by Aurelio Villatoro in the Huehuetenango region of Guatemala between 1,800 - 2,000 meters above sea level. Cupping Notes: Honey, floral and citrus with dark chocolate.

name: Guatemala: Decaf HHT Royal Select, Huehuetenango
description: From the mountain forests of Guatemala's Santa Rosa region, this Swiss Water Decaf comes from the historic Finca Sabanetas, a family-run farm producing exceptional coffee for generations. Grown in rich volcanic soil and shaded by fruit trees, these beans develop a clean, vibrant character that shines even after decaffeination. In the cup, expect a sweet, balanced cup with notes of cane sugar, stone fruit, milk chocolate, and roasted hazelnut, finished with a gentle citrus brightness. Decaffeinated using the chemical-free Swiss Water Process.

name: Multi Origin: Decaf Morning Glory, Multi Origin Blend
cupping_notes: Citrus, bright, good body, milk chocolate sweetness, balanced, less decaf taste.
description: Morning Glory Swiss Water Process Decaf will become one of our best selling Decafs! A unique blend of South & Central American coffees with a hint of Indonesian coffees decaffeinated using the Swiss Water Process. This outstanding decaf is a multiple-origin blend named in honor of that lovely blue flower that blooms before sunrise, is vibrant all day and calls it quits by sundown. You might just say this coffee is for folks who are all about some shut eye, come nightfall. Morning Glory Decaf is decaffeinated by Swiss Water Process, which uses water to create a coffee that’s 99.9 percent caffeine free. Cupping notes : Citrus, bright, good body, milk chocolate sweetness, balanced, less decaf taste.

name: Honduras: Organic 18 Rabbit Washed, Marcala
cupping_notes: Chocolate and caramel aromas with chocolate flavors and a mild green apple-like acidity with a heavy body and very sweet.
description: 18 Rabbit––part of Honduras’ Cup of Excellence––is a collection of farms owned by Señora Flhor, her mother, and eleven members of their family. As pioneers of organic and biodynamic coffee-farming techniques, the soil they use is always naturally regenerated. 18 Rabbit Washed coffees are grown in the Marcala region and wash-processed, which gives the roast a sweet flavor. Cupping Notes: Chocolate and caramel aromas with chocolate flavors and a mild green apple-like acidity with a heavy body and very sweet.

name: Honduras: Organic 18 Rabbit Natural, Marcala
cupping_notes: Strawberry aromas that carry over into the cup with fruit forward flavors, hints of chocolate, and a thin body-well balanced.
description: Señora Flhor refers to the 18 Rabbit Natural as her “crunchberry” coffee due to the sweet flavor it develops after natural processing––a back-to-basics approach stemming from Ethiopia also known as “dry processing.” In natural processing, the fruit is left on the bean and the coffee is barely disrupted while drying. This process differs from washed coffee because naturally processed beans are sun-dried with the cherry intact. The 18 Rabbit Naturals are grown on their namesake farmland family-owned by Señora Flhor, her mother, and 11 other relatives. 18 Rabbit’s beans are grown on a micro-lot in the Marcala region, and roasts well at medium (crisp) or dark (sweet). Cupping notes: Strawberry aromas that carry over into the cup with fruit forward flavors, hints of chocolate, and a thin body-well balanced.

name: CBC Blend: Verso l'Alto Blend
cupping_notes: Chocolate, brown sugar, tangerine
description: NEW BLEND! Cupping notes: Chocolate, brown sugar, tangerine

name: CBC Blend: Kope Kapuna
description: Our Kope Kapuna combination was a 2007 Holiday hit. So rather than keeping the secret limited edition, we decided to make it permanent in our offerings. Russ concocted this bean combo with plenty of Hawaiian flair and nostalgia. In keeping with the season's pleasures, the Kope Kapuna blend is chocolatey, fruity, and spicy. It’s perfect for a chilly holiday morning––and now, every morning! Year-round, this is our special offering to you. Add your roasting results and tips to the product reviews/comments for everyone to share.

name: Honduras: Organic 18 Rabbit Red, Marcala
cupping_notes: Aromas of strawberry, raspberry, and cherry that carry over into the cup with a heavier body and mild fruit notes of graham cracker, and walnuts. Balanced acidity and sweetness, well rounded, smooth, and juicy.
description: The name “Honey Process” actually comes from how sticky the beans get during processing. This type of processing coffee beans is halfway between a washed coffee and a natural process coffee: it’s fruity, but not in as exaggerated a way as some naturals. It often has a more rounded acidity than washed coffees, with intense sweetness and complex mouthfeel. Typically, the more mucilage left on the bean, the sweeter the taste. Subcategories have developed based on the amount of mucilage that is left as well as their drying times: yellow, red, golden, black, and white honey. 18 Rabbit is a collective of farms in Honduras that are female owned by Senora Flhor, her mother, and different members of the Zelaya Ontreras family. Dulce Marlen, the owner of Finca Dulce Luna, is the matriarch of the family, and owner of 18 Rabbit exports. She and her husband paved the way for organic and biodynamic farming practices, being intentional about naturally regenerating the soil they use for their agriculture. Members of this family have placed in the top 10 for Honduras' Cup of Excellence, and work together to create these unique fermentations you'll find in these coffees. The Red Honey Process is fermented for 24 hours, and mostly at night in the cool weather. The cooler weather creates a slower ferment that you can taste in this coffee. Cupping Notes: Aromas of strawberry, raspberry, and cherry that carry over into the cup with a heavier body and mild fruit notes of graham cracker, and walnuts. Balanced acidity and sweetness, well rounded, smooth, and juicy.

name: Panama: Janson Farms Geisha, Volcan High Lands
cupping_notes: Balanced, juicy, crisp, mild, and smooth with flavor notes of milk chocolate, caramel, orange blossom, lemon, black cherry
description: Panama Geisha- 531 This Panama Geisha comes from the Janson Coffee Farm which is located in the Talamanca Mountain Range near the Tisingal and Baru volcanoes in Volcan, Panama. It is a family owned Hacienda that was established in 1941 by Carl Axel Janson. The farm's main focus is quality production. No pesticides, no herbicides! The balance of nutrients in the soil comes from using enzyme micro organisms. This farm is committed to improve and protect the environment by using solar panels to produce the energy for the farm, reusing all excess matter from processing for fuel and fertilizer, and seeds from the forests are planted in the nursery for reforestation and protection of water resources. Natural spring water is used for their washed processing. The Janson's processing plant was built in 1993. It was designed specifically for specialty coffee. They do Natural and Washed processing with updated technology added to artisanal methods to achieve the quality you will experience in this delicious bean! Cupping notes: Balanced, juicy, crisp, mild, and smooth with flavor notes of milk chocolate, caramel, orange blossom, lemon, black cherry

name: Bali: Kintamani Highlands
cupping_notes: Cherry, grape, jam, and wine
description: The eruption of the Gunung Agung Volcano in 1963 caused a delay in the progress of modern-day coffee cultivation in Indonesia, causing the government to enact programs in the 1970’s and 1980’s to help rejuvenate coffee production. With the distribution of coffee seedlings to local farmers, an island-wide coffee growing campaign in Bali began. Today, the coffee growing area in Bali is an estimated 7,500 hectares. The Kintamani highlands, where most coffee is grown, sits atop a large volcanic plateau at 1,300 meters above sea level. Coffee tree varieties include a high percentage of Bourbon and Typica, along with shade trees such as Erythrina, Albizia, tangerine and orange. The use of pesticides is prohibited on Bali and all fertilizers are 100% organic. The Subak Abian is a traditional farming structure organization in Bali, similar to a farmer cooperative. There are 13 different Subak Abians that are currently growing and processing coffee. The “SA” oversee both agricultural technology and religious activities. The promotion of improved coffee growing practices is expected to enhance not only agricultural technology but social and economic standing in Bali as well. Cupping notes : Cherry, grape, jam, and wine

name: Colombia: Cattleya,Excelso
cupping_notes: Well balanced, bright, complex acidity, citrus, grapefruit, floral, roasted nut and cocoa, good body, clean finish
description: Named after Colombia's national flower , Cattleya is a coffee that embodies the beauty, balance, and elegance of one of the world's most celebrated coffee origins. This carefully crafted offering highlights everything coffee lovers appreciate about Colombian coffees—bright acidity, smooth sweetness, and delicate floral complexity. Cattleya is sourced from a network of dedicated smallholder farmers in the Tequendama region of Cundinamarca and the Lengupá province of Boyacá . By selecting coffees from multiple producers, each harvest is blended to maintain a dependable flavor profile while celebrating the unique character of Colombia's Eastern Andes. Cupping Notes: Well balanced, bright, complex acidity, citrus, grapefruit, floral, roasted nut and cocoa, good body, clean finish

name: Papua New Guinea: Arokara AA, Eastern Highlands
cupping_notes: dark chocolate, ripe plum, and earthy tones, balanced by a creamy body and wine-like acidity Learn more about PNG coffee beans with our dedicated guide.
description: Grown in the Eastern Highlands of Papua New Guinea, Arokara AA and AX coffees come from the Arokara Cooperative and its network of local plantations, including Tairora and Gadsup. Today, these farms are owned and managed by their original landowner groups, who cultivate coffee without chemical fertilizers or pesticides. Cherries are hand-picked by the local clans, pulped the same day, and fermented for approximately 36 hours before being washed with fresh mountain stream water from the Aru River. The coffee is then sun-dried for 7–12 days, developing the distinctive bluish appearance associated with coffees from the region. Papua New Guinea’s rugged mountains and diverse coffee-growing communities create coffees known for vibrant acidity, complexity, and a distinctive character. Many local producers grow coffee in traditional “coffee gardens”—small plots often cultivated alongside subsistence crops. Arokara reflects this unique farming heritage while benefiting from careful, consistent processing. Cupping Notes: dark chocolate, ripe plum, and earthy tones, balanced by a creamy body and wine-like acidity Learn more about PNG coffee beans with our dedicated guide.

name: Bolivia: Organic Apolo, La Paz Department
cupping_notes: Transparent citrus and tangerine acidity. With remarkable clarity, complexity, and creaminess.
description: Apolo is an indigenous region of Northern Bolivia that had never commercially grown or exported coffee, until they began working with Wildlife Conservation Society and Cafe Kreyol in order to create a model of ecological preservation, and economic sustainable income. Cafe Kreyol works directly with 5 indigenous communities of Apolo, that speak a form of Quechua that predates the Incas. The coffee from this region, with a very defined orange acidity (when roasted light), chocolatey flavor, and sweet aroma, is quickly taking it’s place as one of the top coffees of Bolivia. Cupping notes: Transparent citrus and tangerine acidity. With remarkable clarity, complexity, and creaminess.

name: Red Sea
cupping_notes: Fruity characteristics of ripe red fruits with bright acidity and earthy undertones
description: An exciting, complex blend of Ethiopian and Yemen dry-processed beans! These two countries rest on opposite sides of the Red Sea, hence the name of this delicious mix. For those who prefer lighter roasts, this coffee will show excellent bright, ripe red fruits and berries. Once pushed to second crack, the beans develop a unique roasted fruit profile due to their birthplace––the high mountains Cupping Notes: Fruity characteristics of ripe red fruits with bright acidity and earthy undertones

name: Sulawesi: Kalossi, Tana Toraja
cupping_notes: Intense flavor with a smooth, creamy medium-to-full body. Sweet brown sugar and honey aromas introduce mild, crisp acidity complemented by notes of citrus, orange, nectarine, cherries, brown spice, and dark chocolate. Finishes with a clean, sweet, lingering aftertaste.
description: Arrival date: Ealry October On Sulawesi, the Indonesian island previously known as Celebes, "Kalossi" was the former Dutch name for the island. It predates "Toraja" as a name for this coffee. The producers in this region have many favorable conditions for growing coffee, such as volcanic soil and thick forests for shade that maintain the moisture needed by the coffee plants. Small family farms grow and process their own coffee cherries, using the wet-hulled method that leaves the beans exposed as they dry on patios. They are then collected and transported to a central dry mill for final preparation, sorting, and export. Cupping Notes: Intense flavor with a smooth, creamy medium-to-full body. Sweet brown sugar and honey aromas introduce mild, crisp acidity complemented by notes of citrus, orange, nectarine, cherries, brown spice, and dark chocolate. Finishes with a clean, sweet, lingering aftertaste.

name: Guatemala La Flor del Cafe Antigua Peaberry
cupping_notes: Lively acidity and a heavy body with flavors of chocolate and caramel.
description: This Peaberry comes from the Pastores mill in the heart of Antigua up to 1,600 meters above sea level on small farms. It is the same version of our La Flor del Cafe, only the peaberries are sorted out. Coming from one of the world's top coffee growing regions, Guatemala, the quality control is impeccable, with only the absolute cream of the crop chosen for export. Cupping Notes: Lively acidity and a heavy body with flavors of chocolate and caramel.

name: CBC Blend: Citrus Sting
cupping_notes: Milk chocolate, orange citrus, fresh cracked pepper Fine replacement for the retired HIGHLANDS blend!
description: Crafted by our own Scorpio, the Citrus Sting is a blend of Indonesian, South American, and Central American coffee. Made for a bold drip brew for daily drinkers. Bringing the bold spice of an Indonesian traditional process and 2 compelling Latin-American washed coffees, this blend creates a well-balanced, chocolaty cup with a citrus twist and a peppery spice note. Cupping Notes: Milk chocolate, orange citrus, fresh cracked pepper Fine replacement for the retired HIGHLANDS blend!

name: Peru: Organic Decaf Sol Y Cafe, Cajamarca
cupping_notes: bright acidity, smooth body, and flavor notes of citrus and floral to cocoa and caramel.
description: Cooperativa de Servicios Multiples Sol y Café Ltda (Coop Sol y Café) was established in March of 2008 to unite over 1,000 farmers. This included rice and cacao producers. The co-op was originally formed to collectively make agronomic and economic decisions. One of their objectives was to protect the environment, and to help communities and their families to develop and progress. They continue to work towards the sustainability of their crops and future development by maintaining their Organic and Fair Trade certifications. Cupping Notes: bright acidity, smooth body, and flavor notes of citrus and floral to cocoa and caramel.

name: Costa Rica: Romelia SHB, Palmichal
cupping_notes: Milk chocolate, citrus, caramel, green apple. Bright acidity, creamy body
description: Romelia SHB EP comes from the cloud-covered Palmichal rainforest, right on the edge of Tarrazú and known for its buttery smooth acidity. The region owes its coffee legacy to Manuel Rojas Arias, who pioneered growing here and founded Beneficio Palmichal in 1933 — the same year he processed a prize-winning 5,025 bags of SHB coffee. When he passed, he left the farm to his sister Romelia, whose strength kept the quality alive. This EP-grade lot is hand-sorted on top of optical sorting for a clean, defect-free cup. Its mild flavor profile and rich, creamy body make this a wonderful blending coffee. Cupping notes : Milk chocolate, citrus, caramel, green apple. Bright acidity, creamy body

name: Uganda: Kaweri Robusta, Mubende
cupping_notes: Peanut, popcorn, salted caramel, vanilla, slightly floral, pear, malty, quick finish, light body.
description: This premium Ugandan robusta is grown on the Kaweri farm, which cultivates 1,626 hectares of selected Ugandan coffee under indigenous shade trees. The farm produces high-quality, dense, hard beans comparable to high-grown Arabica and is pioneering the washed process for Robusta in Uganda. Their meticulous harvesting and processing methods include selective cherry picking and a thorough post-harvest process involving pulping, soaking, sun pre-drying, and final drum drying Cupping notes: Peanut, popcorn, salted caramel, vanilla, slightly floral, pear, malty, quick finish, light body.

name: CBC Blend: Big Black
description: This bold organic coffee blend brings out the best of African and Asian coffee beans. African coffees are usually described as complex, fruity and floral. These are stronger, fragrant-rich, and full-bodied flavored beans. Asian coffees tend to be earthier and darker than most other regional blends. These coffees tend to be smooth, dense, and exotic with dark chocolate, bold nuttiness, and subtle earthy tones. We think this coffee is best as a dark roast, but your taste will be the final decider! Let us know how you roasted this variety in the product reviews.
